# Momentum and preservation of the mean field {#sec-momentum}

## Fixed linear memory

In the setup of @sec-controlled-markov-sa, fix $0\leq\alpha<1$ and
introduce an $\R^d$-valued momentum variable with $M_0$ measurable with
respect to $\cF_0$. Replace
@eq-controlled-sa-recursion by

$$
\Momentumupdate
$$ {#eq-momentum-recursion}

and

$$
\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+\gamma_{n+1}M_{n+1}.
$$ {#eq-momentum-sa}

The filtration includes the momentum history, and the observations still
satisfy @eq-controlled-transition. The coefficient $\alpha$ is fixed;
it is not another vanishing SA gain. At $\alpha=0$ the recursion reduces
to the ordinary update.

## Stationary frozen momentum

Fix $\theta$ and use the two-sided stationary frozen chain with path law
$\statlawtheta$ from @sec-controlled-markov-sa. Define its stationary
momentum by

$$
\Mtheta
:=(1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
  \alpha^j\Htheta(X_{-j}^\theta).
$$ {#eq-frozen-momentum}

At $\alpha=0$ this expression means $\Mtheta=\Htheta(X_0^\theta)$.

::: {#lem-stationary-momentum-exists}
## Integrable stationary memory

Fix $\theta$. If the frozen observations are stationary with marginal
$\pitheta$ and $\pitheta(\norm{\Htheta})<\infty$, the series in
@eq-frozen-momentum converges absolutely almost surely and in $L^1$
under $\statlawtheta$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Put $c_\theta:=\int\norm{\Htheta(x)}\,\pitheta(\dd x)<\infty$.
Tonelli's theorem and stationarity give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{
  (1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
  \alpha^j\norm{\Htheta(X_{-j}^\theta)}}
&=(1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\alpha^j c_\theta\\
&=c_\theta.
\end{aligned}
$$

The nonnegative series of norms is consequently finite almost surely.
If $S_J$ denotes the partial sum in @eq-frozen-momentum through $j=J$,
the same bound on its tail gives
$\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\norm{\Mtheta-S_J}}
\leq c_\theta\alpha^{J+1}\to0$. This proves the $L^1$ assertion as well.
:::

## Preservation of the frozen field

::: {#prp-momentum-field}
## Momentum preserves the frozen mean field

For fixed $\theta$ and $0\leq\alpha<1$, suppose the frozen Markov chain
with kernel $\Ptheta$ is stationary with marginal $\pitheta$ and
$\pitheta(\norm{\Htheta})<\infty$. Then the stationary momentum in
@eq-frozen-momentum satisfies

$$
\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Mtheta}=\htheta.
$$ {#eq-momentum-mean-field}

:::

::: {.proof}
The integrable series-of-norms bound in
@lem-stationary-momentum-exists justifies interchanging the sum and
expectation, componentwise. Stationarity and
@eq-stationary-one-step-field then yield

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Mtheta}
&=(1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\alpha^j
  \Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Htheta(X_{-j}^\theta)}\\
&=(1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\alpha^j\htheta\\
&=\htheta.
\end{aligned}
$$

No independence across time is used. The calculation uses only
stationarity, integrability, and the normalisation
$(1-\alpha)\sum_{j\geq0}\alpha^j=1$; indeed, this field identity holds
for any stationary observation sequence with the same marginal and
first-moment bound.
:::

The equality in @eq-momentum-mean-field is stronger than equality of
roots: it leaves the entire frozen first-order Robbins–Monro field
unchanged. In particular,

$$
\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Mtheta}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\htheta=0.
$$

This is a stationary field identification; it does not by itself prove
convergence of the adaptive recursion @eq-momentum-sa.

::: {#rem-momentum-initialisation .remark}
## Initialisation in the frozen system

For frozen stationary observations and any integrable initial $M_0$,
iteration of the frozen recursion gives, for $n\geq1$,

$$
M_n=\alpha^n M_0
+(1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\alpha^j\Htheta(X_{n-j}^\theta).
$$ {#eq-frozen-momentum-unrolling}

Taking expectations and summing the finite geometric series gives

$$
\E[M_n]=\alpha^n\E[M_0]+(1-\alpha^n)\htheta.
$$ {#eq-frozen-momentum-expectation}

Thus $M_0=0$ gives $\E[M_n]=(1-\alpha^n)\htheta$, and the
initialisation bias relative to $\htheta$ decays geometrically. No
independence between $M_0$ and the observations is needed for this
expectation calculation. These are frozen identities; they do not
replace $\theta_n$ by a constant in the actual adaptive recursion.
:::

## An alternative augmented-state interpretation

The augmented-state construction is not needed to prove
@prp-momentum-field. That identity follows directly from stationarity
and linearity, with the interchange justified by integrability.
Augmentation instead provides a stronger structural interpretation:
by adjoining the memory state, the history-dependent momentum algorithm
can be written again as an ordinary controlled Markov stochastic
approximation recursion.

When $\alpha>0$, the readout in @eq-momentum-recursion depends on the
stored $M_n$ and is generally not a one-step observable of $X_{n+1}$
alone. Set $Y_n:=(X_n,M_n)\in\StateSpace\times\R^d$. The frozen
augmented kernel is

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_\theta((x,m),\dd x'\,\dd m')
&=\Pkern{\theta}{x}{\dd x'}\,
  \delta_{\alpha m+(1-\alpha)\Htheta(x')}(\dd m').
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-momentum-augmented-kernel}

The Dirac factor records the deterministic momentum update after the
new observation is drawn. With readout $G_{\mathrm m}(x,m):=m$,
@eq-momentum-recursion and @eq-momentum-sa become

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_{n+1}\mid\cF_n&\sim Q_{\theta_n}(Y_n,\cdot),\\
\theta_{n+1}
&=\theta_n+\gamma_{n+1}G_{\mathrm m}(Y_{n+1}).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-momentum-augmented-sa}

Thus the memory update is represented as a Markov recursion on an
enlarged state space. To describe its stationary lift, apply the
filter in @eq-frozen-momentum at each integer time, defining
$M_k^\theta:=(1-\alpha)\sum_{j\geq0}\alpha^j
\Htheta(X_{k-j}^\theta)$, with $M_0^\theta=\Mtheta$.
The series converge simultaneously for all $k\in\mathbb Z$ outside one
null set. Shifting indices in these absolutely convergent series gives

$$
M_{k+1}^\theta
=\alpha M_k^\theta+(1-\alpha)\Htheta(X_{k+1}^\theta).
$$ {#eq-frozen-momentum-recursion}

::: {#prp-momentum-stationary-lift}
## An invariant lift of the frozen path law

Under the hypotheses of @prp-momentum-field, define

$$
\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}
:=\Law_{\statlawtheta}(X_0^\theta,\Mtheta).
$$ {#eq-momentum-stationary-law}

Then $\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}$ is invariant for $Q_\theta$ and
$\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}(G_{\mathrm m})=\htheta$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Put $Y_k^\theta:=(X_k^\theta,M_k^\theta)$. The map from the base
trajectory to $Y_k^\theta$ is the same measurable history functional
shifted by $k$. Shift stationarity of the base path therefore makes
$(Y_k^\theta)_{k\in\mathbb Z}$ stationary.

Moreover, $M_0^\theta$ is measurable with respect to
$\mathcal H_0^\theta:=\sigma(X_k^\theta:k\leq0)$.
Conditional on this past, $X_1^\theta$ has law
$\Pkern{\theta}{X_0^\theta}{\cdot}$, and $M_1^\theta$ is determined
by @eq-frozen-momentum-recursion. Hence, for every bounded measurable
$u:\StateSpace\times\R^d\to\R$,
$\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{u(Y_1^\theta)\mid\mathcal H_0^\theta}
=Q_\theta u(Y_0^\theta)$. Integrating this identity and using
stationarity gives

$$
\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}(Q_\theta u)
=\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{u(Y_1^\theta)}
=\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}(u),
$$

which proves invariance. The readout is integrable by
@lem-stationary-momentum-exists, and its mean is given by
@eq-momentum-mean-field. No uniqueness assertion is needed.
:::

Starting from the lifted formulation, its ordinary frozen drift is
therefore

$$
\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}(G_{\mathrm m})
=\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Mtheta}
=\htheta.
$$ {#eq-momentum-lifted-field}

This gives an alternative identification of the same Robbins–Monro
field and its roots, already obtained by the direct filter calculation.
The two routes have different purposes:

- **Route A: direct stationary filter.** Take the expectation of
  @eq-frozen-momentum to obtain @eq-momentum-mean-field; no augmented
  kernel is needed.
- **Route B: augmented-state lift.** Pass from $\Ptheta$ to $Q_\theta$,
  construct the invariant law $\nu_\theta^{\mathrm{mom}}$, and average
  $G_{\mathrm m}$ to recover @eq-momentum-lifted-field. This supplies
  the stronger structural formulation; using it to establish adaptive
  convergence requires additional analysis.

### Discussion point: augmented-state lifting

A possible stronger route is to treat the momentum recursion as a
controlled Markov stochastic approximation on the enlarged state
$Y_n=(X_n,M_n)$. This is not needed to establish
@prp-momentum-field: preservation of the frozen Robbins–Monro field
follows directly from stationarity and linearity. The stronger question
is whether assumptions on the base frozen family $\Ptheta$ can be
transferred to the lifted family $Q_\theta$ strongly enough to invoke
an existing controlled-Markov SA theorem. Relevant properties would
include invariant-law, mixing or coupling, Poisson-equation, and
parameter-regularity estimates. We leave this as a discussion point.
